title: Phasebook: hierarchical release conductor with traffic-slicing lanes and automatic reclamation
author: Priya Khatri
description: Summary: Introduces 'Phasebook', a hierarchical release conductor that coordinates multi-lane traffic slicing, policy-driven holdpoints, and an automatic reclamation path that reclaims capacity from failed lanes and fast-rolls back with an explainable decision trace. Motivation: customers running complex A/B experiments and phased canaries asked for a simpler way to define layered release strategies (global -> region -> cohort) plus automatic reclamation when a lane breaches SLOs; engineers were repeatedly wiring similar logic in pipelines which created fragility and telemetry gaps. This PR implements the conductor runtime, a small declarative DSL for lanes and policies, and integrations for telemetry, replay, and rollback. What changed: 1) New runtime: phasebook/conductor with lane graph executor, safety gate evaluator, and reclamation engine. 2) DSL: phasebook/config schema (YAML) to declare hierarchical lanes, slice selectors, SLO gates, and reclaim policies. 3) Control-plane API: additions to /v1/releases to accept phasebook manifests and progress queries. 4) Telemetry hooks: per-lane tracing spans, a new lane_reclamation metric, and Grafana dashboards links in the README. 5) Test harness: deterministic replay + mini-replay simulator that can exercise reclamation and backfill traces for offline validation. 6) Migration: backward-compatible; older release schemas still supported. Key behaviors: - Traffic-slicing lanes are hierarchical: top-level global lane -> region lanes -> cohort lanes. - Each lane has SLO gates (latency, error_rate, quality_regression) evaluated against streaming metrics; if gate trips, lane enters Reclaiming state. - Reclamation policy can be immediate (drain and revert) or gradual (fractional drain + replay sampling). - All reclamation actions produce an explainable decision trace stored in release history for audit. Rolling this out: initial rollout only for internal/experimental releases (flag: enable_phasebook). We will run 2 staging experiments then flip the guard. Testing & validation: - Unit tests for gate evaluation and lane graph transitions. - Integration tests in perf-canary environment using synthetic traffic shapes. - Deterministic replay tests that assert invariant: total traffic fraction conserved during progressive reclaim. - Smoke end-to-end with the /v1/releases API, and post-merge canary to 1% traffic in prod; abort on any SLO breach. Related work items: Linear ENG-2141 (phasebook design), ENG-2210 (reclamation telemetry), PM-78 (release UX). See linked files for config examples. Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag. 2) Internal canary: 1% global traffic for 48h. 3) Staged expansion to 5% then 20% with human gates. 4) Enable for self-serve after 2 weeks and additional telemetry coverage. Backwards compatibility: existing release manifests remain valid; the conductor only activates for manifests that declare phasebook DSL. Migration notes included in docs/phasebook-migration.md. Security considerations: API uses existing release ACLs; reclamation traces are audited via existing audit log sink. Observability: New Grafana dashboard panels (links included) plus lane_reclamation counter and decision_trace span. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-2141) linked - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] E2E smoke test script included - [x] Docs and migration notes - [x] Feature flag gated - [x] Telemetry dashboards added Commits (summary): - feat(conductor): add phasebook runtime and lane graph executor - feat(api): accept phasebook manifests at /v1/releases - feat(dsl): add phasebook YAML schema and validation - feat(telemetry): lane_reclamation metric & tracing hooks - test(replay): deterministic replay harness and integration tests - docs(phasebook): migration guide and dashboard links Files changed (high level): - src/conductor/phasebook_executor.go - src/api/releases_phasebook_handler.go - proto/releases/v1/phasebook.proto - configs/phasebook/examples/sample_manifest.yaml - infra/telemetry/dashboards/phasebook.json - tools/replay/mini_replay_simulator.py - docs/phasebook-migration.md - test/integration/phasebook_e2e_test.go Why this is safe: the feature is behind enable_phasebook and will not affect existing releases. All external API changes are additive. Reclamation paths only modify traffic assignment; no model artifacts are deleted. Observability and audit traces ensure actions are reconstructible. Migration and rollback strategy: reclamation records and decision traces are persisted, and manual overrides via the /v1/releases/{id}/abort endpoint are supported. Rollback is reversible because underlying model versions are unchanged and traffic assignments are updated atomically. Notes for reviewers: focus on gate evaluation correctness, edge-case transitions (overlapping gates in nested lanes), and race conditions in reclamation (concurrent reclaim/expand). CI: See checks summary below. Merge method: squash and merge with linear history disabled.

review_comments: Daniel Huang: Gate evaluation looks solid, but we need an explicit test for concurrent reclaim + promote race (see test suggestion).

Elliot Graves: Telemetry thresholds look aggressive for noisy regions; recommending smoothing (moving average) in gate evaluator.
